href="./Category:Articles_needing_additional_references_from_January_2009"/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_needing_additional_references"/></span>
<p id="mwBA">In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database" title="Database" id="mwBQ">database</a> systems, <b id="mwBg">isolation</b> is one of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID" title="ACID" id="mwBw">ACID</a> (<i id="mwCA"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomicity_(database_systems)" title="Atomicity (database systems)" id="mwCQ">Atomicity</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consistency_(database_systems)" title="Consistency (database systems)" id="mwCg">Consistency</a>, Isolation, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durability_(database_systems)" title="Durability (database systems)" id="mwCw">Durability</a></i>) <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_transaction" title="Database transaction" id="mwDA">transaction</a> properties. It determines how <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_transaction" title="Database transaction" id="mwDQ">transaction</a> integrity is visible to other users and systems. A lower isolation level increases the ability of many users to access the same data at the same time, but also increases the number of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_(computer_science)" title="Concurrency (computer science)" id="mwDg">concurrency</a> effects (such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Write–read_conflict" title="Write–read conflict" id="mwDw"> dirty reads</a> or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_update" title="Lost update" class="mw-redirect" id="mwEA">lost updates</a>) users might encounter. Conversely, a higher isolation level reduces the types of concurrency effects that users may encounter, but requires more system resources and increases the chances that one transaction will block another.<sup about="#mwt4" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-1"}}'><a href="#cite_note-1" id="mwEQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEw">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwFA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwFQ" data-mw='{"autoGenerated":true}'/></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwFg" aria-labelledby="DBMS_concurrency_control"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="DBMS_concurrency_control">DBMS concurrency control</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: DBMS concurrency control"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwFw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_control" title="Concurrency control" id="mwGA">Concurrency control</a> comprises the underlying mechanisms in a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DBMS" title="DBMS" class="mw-redirect" id="mwGQ">DBMS</a> which handle isolation and guarantee related correctness. It is heavily used by the database and storage engines both to guarantee the correct execution of concurrent transactions, and (via different mechanisms) the correctness of other DBMS processes. The transaction-related mechanisms typically constrain the database data access operations' timing (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_transaction_schedule" title="Database transaction schedule" id="mwGg">transaction schedules</a>) to certain orders characterized as the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serializability" title="Serializability" class="mw-redirect" id="mwGw">serializability</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recoverability" title="Recoverability" class="mw-redirect" id="mwHA">recoverability</a> schedule properties. Constraining database access operation execution typically means reduced performance (measured by rates of execution), and thus concurrency control mechanisms are typically designed to provide the best performance possible under the constraints. Often, when possible without harming correctness, the serializability property is compromised for better performance. However, recoverability cannot be compromised, since such typically results in a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_integrity" title="Data integrity" id="mwHQ">database integrity violation</a>.</p>

<p id="mwHg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-phase_locking" title="Two-phase locking" id="mwHw">Two-phase locking</a> is the most common transaction concurrency control method in DBMSs, used to provide both serializability and recoverability for correctness. In order to access a database object a transaction first needs to acquire a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lock_(database)" title="Lock (database)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwIA">lock</a> for this object. Depending on the access operation type (e.g., reading or writing an object) and on the lock type, acquiring the lock may be blocked and postponed, if another transaction is holding a lock for that object.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwIQ" aria-labelledby="Client-side_isolation"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Client-side_isolation">Client-side isolation</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Client-side isolation"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwIg">Isolation is typically enforced at the database level. However, various client-side systems can also be used. It can be controlled in application frameworks or runtime containers such as <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J2EE" title="J2EE" class="mw-redirect" id="mwIw">J2EE</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entity_Bean" title="Entity Bean" id="mwJA">Entity Beans</a><sup about="#mwt6" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Stony_Brook_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Stony Brook"}}'><a href="#cite_note-Stony_Brook-2" id="mwJQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwJg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKA">]</span></span></a></sup> On older systems, it may be implemented systemically (by the application developers), for example through the use of temporary tables.<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_failed_verification" about="#mwt5" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwKQ" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Failed verification","href":"./Template:Failed_verification"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"March 2024"},"reason":{"wt":"The paragraph source does not mention temporary tables."}},"i":0}}]}'/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_failed_verification_from_March_2024" about="#mwt5"/><sup class="noprint Inline-Template " style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt5" id="mwKg"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability" title="Wikipedia:Verifiability"><span title="The paragraph source does not mention temporary tables. (March 2024)">failed verification</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> In two-tier, three-tier, or <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multitier_architecture" title="Multitier architecture" id="mwKw">n-tier</a> web applications a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transaction_manager" title="Transaction manager" class="mw-redirect" id="mwLA">transaction manager</a> can be used to maintain isolation. A transaction manager is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middleware_(distributed_applications)" title="Middleware (distributed applications)" id="mwLQ">middleware</a> which sits between an app service (back-end application service) and the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system" title="Operating system" id="mwLg">operating system</a>. A transaction manager can provide global isolation and atomicity. It tracks when new servers join a transaction and coordinates an <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_commit" title="Atomic commit" id="mwLw">atomic commit</a> protocol among the servers. The details are abstracted from the app, making transactions simpler and easier to code. A <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transaction_processing_system" title="Transaction processing system" id="mwMA">transaction processing monitor</a> (TPM) is a collection of middle-ware including a transaction manager. A TPM might provide local isolation to an app with a lock manager.<sup about="#mwt7" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Stony_Brook_2-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Stony Brook"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Stony_Brook-2"}}'><a href="#cite_note-Stony_Brook-2" id="mwMQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwMg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwNA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwNQ" aria-labelledby="Read_phenomena"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Read_phenomena">Read phenomena</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Read phenomena"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwNg">The ANSI/ISO standard SQL 92 refers to three different <i id="mwNw">read phenomena</i> when a transaction retrieves data that another transaction might have updated.</p>

<p id="mwOA">In the following examples, two transactions take place. In transaction 1, a query is performed, then in transaction 2, an update is performed, and finally in transaction 1, the same query is performed again.</p>

<p id="mwOQ">The examples use the following relation:</p>

<table class="wikitable" id="mwOg">
<caption id="mwOw">users</caption>
<tbody id="mwPA"><tr id="mwPQ"><th id="mwPg">id</th><th id="mwPw">name</th><th id="mwQA">age</th></tr>
<tr id="mwQQ">
<td id="mwQg">1</td><td id="mwQw">Alice</td><td id="mwRA">20</td></tr>
<tr id="mwRQ">
<td id="mwRg">2</td><td id="mwRw">Bob</td><td id="mwSA">25</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwSQ" aria-labelledby="Dirty_reads"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Dirty_reads">Dirty reads</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Dirty reads"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt8" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwSg" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Main","href":"./Template:Main"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Write-read conflict"}},"i":0}}]}'><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1368532237" typeof="mw:Extension/templatestyles" about="#mwt9" data-mw='{"name":"templatestyles","attrs":{"src":"Module:Hatnote/styles.css"},"body":{"extsrc":""}}'>.mw-parser-output .hatnote{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output div.hatnote{padding-left:1.6em;margin-bottom:0.5em}.mw-parser-output .hatnote i{font-style:normal}.mw-parser-output .hatnote+.mw-empty-elt+.hatnote{margin-top:-0.5em}@media print{body.ns-0 .mw-parser-output .hatnote{display:none!important}}</style></span><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable" about="#mwt8" id="mwSw">Main article: <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Write-read_conflict" title="Write-read conflict" class="mw-redirect">Write-read conflict</a></div>

<p id="mwTA">A <i id="mwTQ">dirty read</i> (aka <i id="mwTg">uncommitted dependency</i>) occurs when a transaction retrieves a row that has been updated by another transaction that is not yet committed.</p>

<p id="mwTw">In this example, transaction 1 retrieves the row with id 1, then transaction 2 updates the row with id 1, and finally transaction 1 retrieves the row with id 1 again. Now if transaction 2 rolls back its update (already retrieved by transaction 1) or performs other updates, then the view of the row may be wrong in transaction 1. At the READ UNCOMMITTED isolation level, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the updated row: this is a dirty read. At the READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, and SERIALIZABLE isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the initial row.</p>

<table id="mwUA">
<tbody id="mwUQ"><tr id="mwUg">
<th id="mwUw">Transaction 1</th>
<th id="mwVA">Transaction 2</th></tr>
<tr id="mwVQ">
<td id="mwVg"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt10" id="mwVw" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nBEGIN;\nSELECT age FROM users WHERE id = 1;\n-- retrieves 20\n"}}'><pre id="mwWA"><span id="mwWQ"></span><span class="k" id="mwWg">BEGIN</span><span class="p" id="mwWw">;</span>
<span class="k" id="mwXA">SELECT</span><span class="w" id="mwXQ"> </span><span class="n" id="mwXg">age</span><span class="w" id="mwXw"> </span><span class="k" id="mwYA">FROM</span><span class="w" id="mwYQ"> </span><span class="n" id="mwYg">users</span><span class="w" id="mwYw"> </span><span class="k" id="mwZA">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mwZQ"> </span><span class="n" id="mwZg">id</span><span class="w" id="mwZw"> </span><span class="o" id="mwaA">=</span><span class="w" id="mwaQ"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwag">1</span><span class="p" id="mwaw">;</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwbA">-- retrieves 20</span>
</pre></div></td>
<td id="mwbQ"></td></tr>
<tr id="mwbg">
<td id="mwbw"></td>
<td id="mwcA"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt11" id="mwcQ" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nBEGIN;\nUPDATE users SET age = 21 WHERE id = 1;\n-- no commit here\n"}}'><pre id="mwcg"><span id="mwcw"></span><span class="k" id="mwdA">BEGIN</span><span class="p" id="mwdQ">;</span>
<span class="k" id="mwdg">UPDATE</span><span class="w" id="mwdw"> </span><span class="n" id="mweA">users</span><span class="w" id="mweQ"> </span><span class="k" id="mweg">SET</span><span class="w" id="mwew"> </span><span class="n" id="mwfA">age</span><span class="w" id="mwfQ"> </span><span class="o" id="mwfg">=</span><span class="w" id="mwfw"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwgA">21</span><span class="w" id="mwgQ"> </span><span class="k" id="mwgg">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mwgw"> </span><span class="n" id="mwhA">id</span><span class="w" id="mwhQ"> </span><span class="o" id="mwhg">=</span><span class="w" id="mwhw"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwiA">1</span><span class="p" id="mwiQ">;</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwig">-- no commit here</span>
</pre></div></td></tr>
<tr id="mwiw">
<td id="mwjA"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt12" id="mwjQ" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nSELECT age FROM users WHERE id = 1;\n-- READ UNCOMMITTED retrieves 21 (dirty read)\n-- READ COMMITTED retrieves 20 (dirty read has been avoided)\n-- REPEATABLE READ retrieves 20 (dirty read has been avoided)\n-- SERIALIZABLE retrieves 20 (dirty read has been avoided)\nCOMMIT;\n"}}'><pre id="mwjg"><span id="mwjw"></span><span class="k" id="mwkA">SELECT</span><span class="w" id="mwkQ"> </span><span class="n" id="mwkg">age</span><span class="w" id="mwkw"> </span><span class="k" id="mwlA">FROM</span><span class="w" id="mwlQ"> </span><span class="n" id="mwlg">users</span><span class="w" id="mwlw"> </span><span class="k" id="mwmA">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mwmQ"> </span><span class="n" id="mwmg">id</span><span class="w" id="mwmw"> </span><span class="o" id="mwnA">=</span><span class="w" id="mwnQ"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwng">1</span><span class="p" id="mwnw">;</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwoA">-- READ UNCOMMITTED retrieves 21 (dirty read)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwoQ">-- READ COMMITTED retrieves 20 (dirty read has been avoided)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwog">-- REPEATABLE READ retrieves 20 (dirty read has been avoided)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwow">-- SERIALIZABLE retrieves 20 (dirty read has been avoided)</span>
<span class="k" id="mwpA">COMMIT</span><span class="p" id="mwpQ">;</span>
</pre></div></td>
<td id="mwpg"></td></tr>
<tr id="mwpw">
<td id="mwqA"></td>
<td id="mwqQ"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt13" id="mwqg" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nROLLBACK;\n"}}'><pre id="mwqw"><span id="mwrA"></span><span class="k" id="mwrQ">ROLLBACK</span><span class="p" id="mwrg">;</span>
</pre></div></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwrw" aria-labelledby="Non-repeatable_reads"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Non-repeatable_reads">Non-repeatable reads</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Non-repeatable reads"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwsA">A <i id="mwsQ">non-repeatable read</i> occurs when a transaction retrieves a row twice and that row is updated by another transaction that is committed in between.</p>

<p id="mwsg">In this example, transaction 1 retrieves the row with id 1, then transaction 2 updates the row with id 1 and is committed, and finally transaction 1 retrieves the row with id 1 again. At the READ UNCOMMITTED and READ COMMITTED isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the updated row: this is a non-repeatable read. At the REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the initial row.</p>

<table id="mwsw">
<tbody id="mwtA"><tr id="mwtQ">
<th id="mwtg">Transaction 1</th>
<th id="mwtw">Transaction 2</th></tr>
<tr id="mwuA">
<td id="mwuQ"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt14" id="mwug" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nBEGIN;\nSELECT age FROM users WHERE id = 1;\n-- retrieves 20\n"}}'><pre id="mwuw"><span id="mwvA"></span><span class="k" id="mwvQ">BEGIN</span><span class="p" id="mwvg">;</span>
<span class="k" id="mwvw">SELECT</span><span class="w" id="mwwA"> </span><span class="n" id="mwwQ">age</span><span class="w" id="mwwg"> </span><span class="k" id="mwww">FROM</span><span class="w" id="mwxA"> </span><span class="n" id="mwxQ">users</span><span class="w" id="mwxg"> </span><span class="k" id="mwxw">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mwyA"> </span><span class="n" id="mwyQ">id</span><span class="w" id="mwyg"> </span><span class="o" id="mwyw">=</span><span class="w" id="mwzA"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwzQ">1</span><span class="p" id="mwzg">;</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwzw">-- retrieves 20</span>
</pre></div></td>
<td id="mw0A"></td></tr>
<tr id="mw0Q">
<td id="mw0g"></td>
<td id="mw0w"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt15" id="mw1A" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nBEGIN;\nUPDATE users SET age = 21 WHERE id = 1;\nCOMMIT;\n"}}'><pre id="mw1Q"><span id="mw1g"></span><span class="k" id="mw1w">BEGIN</span><span class="p" id="mw2A">;</span>
<span class="k" id="mw2Q">UPDATE</span><span class="w" id="mw2g"> </span><span class="n" id="mw2w">users</span><span class="w" id="mw3A"> </span><span class="k" id="mw3Q">SET</span><span class="w" id="mw3g"> </span><span class="n" id="mw3w">age</span><span class="w" id="mw4A"> </span><span class="o" id="mw4Q">=</span><span class="w" id="mw4g"> </span><span class="mi" id="mw4w">21</span><span class="w" id="mw5A"> </span><span class="k" id="mw5Q">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mw5g"> </span><span class="n" id="mw5w">id</span><span class="w" id="mw6A"> </span><span class="o" id="mw6Q">=</span><span class="w" id="mw6g"> </span><span class="mi" id="mw6w">1</span><span class="p" id="mw7A">;</span>
<span class="k" id="mw7Q">COMMIT</span><span class="p" id="mw7g">;</span>
</pre></div></td></tr>
<tr id="mw7w">
<td id="mw8A"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt16" id="mw8Q" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nSELECT age FROM users WHERE id = 1;\n-- READ UNCOMMITTED retrieves 21 (non-repeatable read)\n-- READ COMMITTED retrieves 21 (non-repeatable read)\n-- REPEATABLE READ retrieves 20 (non-repeatable read has been avoided)\n-- SERIALIZABLE retrieves 20 (non-repeatable read has been avoided)\nCOMMIT;\n"}}'><pre id="mw8g"><span id="mw8w"></span><span class="k" id="mw9A">SELECT</span><span class="w" id="mw9Q"> </span><span class="n" id="mw9g">age</span><span class="w" id="mw9w"> </span><span class="k" id="mw-A">FROM</span><span class="w" id="mw-Q"> </span><span class="n" id="mw-g">users</span><span class="w" id="mw-w"> </span><span class="k" id="mw_A">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mw_Q"> </span><span class="n" id="mw_g">id</span><span class="w" id="mw_w"> </span><span class="o" id="mwAQA">=</span><span class="w" id="mwAQE"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwAQI">1</span><span class="p" id="mwAQM">;</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAQQ">-- READ UNCOMMITTED retrieves 21 (non-repeatable read)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAQU">-- READ COMMITTED retrieves 21 (non-repeatable read)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAQY">-- REPEATABLE READ retrieves 20 (non-repeatable read has been avoided)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAQc">-- SERIALIZABLE retrieves 20 (non-repeatable read has been avoided)</span>
<span class="k" id="mwAQg">COMMIT</span><span class="p" id="mwAQk">;</span>
</pre></div></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="6" id="mwAQo" aria-labelledby="Phantom_reads"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Phantom_reads">Phantom reads</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: Phantom reads"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAQs">A <i id="mwAQw">phantom read</i> occurs when a transaction retrieves a set of rows twice and new rows are inserted into or removed from that set by another transaction that is committed in between.</p>

<p id="mwAQ0">In this example, transaction 1 retrieves the set of rows with age greater than 17, then transaction 2 inserts a row with age 26 and is committed, and finally transaction 1 retrieves the set of rows with age greater than 17 again. At the READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, and REPEATABLE READ isolation levels, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the new set of rows that includes the inserted row: this is a phantom read. At the SERIALIZABLE isolation level, the second SELECT in transaction 1 retrieves the initial set of rows.</p>

<table id="mwAQ4">
<tbody id="mwAQ8"><tr id="mwARA">
<th id="mwARE">Transaction 1</th>
<th id="mwARI">Transaction 2</th></tr>
<tr id="mwARM">
<td id="mwARQ"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt17" id="mwARU" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nBEGIN;\nSELECT name FROM users WHERE age > 17;\n-- retrieves Alice and Bob\n"}}'><pre id="mwARY"><span id="mwARc"></span><span class="k" id="mwARg">BEGIN</span><span class="p" id="mwARk">;</span>
<span class="k" id="mwARo">SELECT</span><span class="w" id="mwARs"> </span><span class="n" id="mwARw">name</span><span class="w" id="mwAR0"> </span><span class="k" id="mwAR4">FROM</span><span class="w" id="mwAR8"> </span><span class="n" id="mwASA">users</span><span class="w" id="mwASE"> </span><span class="k" id="mwASI">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mwASM"> </span><span class="n" id="mwASQ">age</span><span class="w" id="mwASU"> </span><span class="o" id="mwASY">></span><span class="w" id="mwASc"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwASg">17</span><span class="p" id="mwASk">;</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwASo">-- retrieves Alice and Bob</span>
</pre></div></td>
<td id="mwASs"></td></tr>
<tr id="mwASw">
<td id="mwAS0"></td>
<td id="mwAS4"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt18" id="mwAS8" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nBEGIN;\nINSERT INTO users VALUES (3, &apos;Carol&apos;, 26);\nCOMMIT;\n"}}'><pre id="mwATA"><span id="mwATE"></span><span class="k" id="mwATI">BEGIN</span><span class="p" id="mwATM">;</span>
<span class="k" id="mwATQ">INSERT</span><span class="w" id="mwATU"> </span><span class="k" id="mwATY">INTO</span><span class="w" id="mwATc"> </span><span class="n" id="mwATg">users</span><span class="w" id="mwATk"> </span><span class="k" id="mwATo">VALUES</span><span class="w" id="mwATs"> </span><span class="p" id="mwATw">(</span><span class="mi" id="mwAT0">3</span><span class="p" id="mwAT4">,</span><span class="w" id="mwAT8"> </span><span class="s1" id="mwAUA">'Carol'</span><span class="p" id="mwAUE">,</span><span class="w" id="mwAUI"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwAUM">26</span><span class="p" id="mwAUQ">);</span>
<span class="k" id="mwAUU">COMMIT</span><span class="p" id="mwAUY">;</span>
</pre></div></td></tr>
<tr id="mwAUc">
<td id="mwAUg"><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-sql mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr" typeof="mw:Extension/syntaxhighlight" about="#mwt19" id="mwAUk" data-mw='{"name":"syntaxhighlight","attrs":{"lang":"sql"},"body":{"extsrc":"\nSELECT name FROM users WHERE age > 17;\n-- READ UNCOMMITTED retrieves Alice, Bob and Carol (phantom read)\n-- READ COMMITTED retrieves Alice, Bob and Carol (phantom read)\n-- REPEATABLE READ retrieves Alice, Bob and Carol (phantom read)\n-- SERIALIZABLE retrieves Alice and Bob (phantom read has been avoided)\nCOMMIT;\n"}}'><pre id="mwAUo"><span id="mwAUs"></span><span class="k" id="mwAUw">SELECT</span><span class="w" id="mwAU0"> </span><span class="n" id="mwAU4">name</span><span class="w" id="mwAU8"> </span><span class="k" id="mwAVA">FROM</span><span class="w" id="mwAVE"> </span><span class="n" id="mwAVI">users</span><span class="w" id="mwAVM"> </span><span class="k" id="mwAVQ">WHERE</span><span class="w" id="mwAVU"> </span><span class="n" id="mwAVY">age</span><span class="w" id="mwAVc"> </span><span class="o" id="mwAVg">></span><span class="w" id="mwAVk"> </span><span class="mi" id="mwAVo">17</span><span class="p" id="mwAVs">;</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAVw">-- READ UNCOMMITTED retrieves Alice, Bob and Carol (phantom read)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAV0">-- READ COMMITTED retrieves Alice, Bob and Carol (phantom read)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAV4">-- REPEATABLE READ retrieves Alice, Bob and Carol (phantom read)</span>
<span class="c1" id="mwAV8">-- SERIALIZABLE retrieves Alice and Bob (phantom read has been avoided)</span>
<span class="k" id="mwAWA">COMMIT</span><span class="p" id="mwAWE">;</span>
</pre></div></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<p id="mwAWI">There are two basic strategies used to prevent non-repeatable reads and phantom reads. In the first strategy, <i id="mwAWM">lock-based concurrency control</i>, transaction 2 is committed after transaction 1 is committed or rolled back. It produces the serial <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_transaction_schedule" title="Database transaction schedule" id="mwAWQ">schedule</a> <i id="mwAWU">T1, T2</i>. In the other strategy, <i id="mwAWY"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiversion_concurrency_control" title="Multiversion concurrency control" id="mwAWc">multiversion concurrency control</a></i>, transaction 2 is committed immediately while transaction 1, which started before transaction 2, continues to operate on an old snapshot of the database taken at the start of transaction 1, and when transaction 1 eventually tries to commit, if the result of committing would be equivalent to the serial schedule <i id="mwAWg">T1, T2</i>, then transaction 1 is committed; otherwise, there is a commit conflict and transaction 1 is rolled back with a serialization failure.</p>

<p id="mwAWk">Under lock-based concurrency control, non-repeatable reads and phantom reads may occur when read locks are not acquired when performing a SELECT, or when the acquired locks on affected rows are released as soon as the SELECT is performed. Under multiversion concurrency control, non-repeatable reads and phantom reads may occur when the requirement that a transaction affected by a commit conflict must be rolled back is relaxed.</p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="7" id="mwAWo" aria-labelledby="Isolation_levels"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Isolation_levels">Isolation levels</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=7" title="Edit section: Isolation levels"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAWs">Of the four <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID" title="ACID" id="mwAWw">ACID</a> properties in a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_management_system" title="Database management system" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAW0">DBMS</a> (Database Management System), the isolation property is the one most often relaxed.  When attempting to maintain the highest level of isolation, a DBMS usually acquires <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lock_(database)" title="Lock (database)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAW4">locks</a> on data which may result in a loss of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_(computer_science)" title="Concurrency (computer science)" id="mwAW8">concurrency</a>, or implements <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiversion_concurrency_control" title="Multiversion concurrency control" id="mwAXA">multiversion concurrency control</a>. This requires adding logic for the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_application" title="Software application" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAXE">application</a> to function correctly.</p>

<p id="mwAXI">Most DBMSs offer a number of <i id="mwAXM">transaction isolation levels</i>, which control the degree of locking that occurs when selecting data. For many database applications, the majority of database transactions can be constructed to avoid requiring high isolation levels (e.g. SERIALIZABLE level), thus reducing the locking overhead for the system.  The programmer must carefully analyze database access code to ensure that any relaxation of isolation does not cause software bugs that are difficult to find. Conversely, if higher isolation levels are used, the possibility of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadlock_(computer_science)" title="Deadlock (computer science)" id="mwAXQ">deadlock</a> is increased, which also requires careful analysis and programming techniques to avoid.</p>

<p id="mwAXU">Since each isolation level is stronger than those below, in that no higher isolation level allows an action forbidden by a lower one, the standard permits a DBMS to run a transaction at an isolation level stronger than that requested (e.g., a "Read committed" transaction may actually be performed at a "Repeatable read" isolation level).</p>

<p id="mwAXY">The isolation levels defined by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_National_Standards_Institute" title="American National Standards Institute" id="mwAXc">ANSI</a>/<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Organization_for_Standardization" title="International Organization for Standardization" id="mwAXg">ISO</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SQL" title="SQL" id="mwAXk">SQL</a> standard are listed as follows.</p>

<section data-mw-section-id="8" id="mwAXo" aria-labelledby="Serializable"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Serializable">Serializable</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=8" title="Edit section: Serializable"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAXs">This is the <i id="mwAXw">highest</i> isolation level.</p>

<p id="mwAX0">With a lock-based <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_control" title="Concurrency control" id="mwAX4">concurrency control</a> DBMS implementation, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serializability" title="Serializability" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAX8">serializability</a> requires read and write locks (acquired on selected data) to be released at the end of the transaction.  Also <i id="mwAYA">range-locks</i> must be acquired when a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Select_(SQL)" title="Select (SQL)" id="mwAYE">SELECT</a> query uses a ranged <i id="mwAYI">WHERE</i> clause, especially to avoid the <i id="mwAYM"><b id="mwAYQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="#Phantom_reads" class="mw-selflink-fragment" id="mwAYU">phantom reads</a></b></i> phenomenon.</p>

<p id="mwAYY">When using non-lock based concurrency control, no locks are acquired; however, if the system detects a <i id="mwAYc">write collision</i> among several concurrent transactions, only one of them is allowed to commit.  See <i id="mwAYg"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapshot_isolation" title="Snapshot isolation" id="mwAYk">snapshot isolation</a></i> for more details on this topic.</p>

<p id="mwAYo">From<span typeof="mw:DisplaySpace" id="mwAYs"> </span>: (Second Informal Review Draft) ISO/IEC 9075:1992, Database Language SQL- July 30, 1992:
<i id="mwAYw">The execution of concurrent SQL-transactions at isolation level SERIALIZABLE is guaranteed to be serializable. A serializable execution is defined to be an execution of the operations of concurrently executing SQL-transactions that produces the same effect as some serial execution of those same SQL-transactions. A serial execution is one in which each SQL-transaction executes to completion before the next SQL-transaction begins.</i></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="9" id="mwAY0" aria-labelledby="Repeatable_reads"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Repeatable_reads">Repeatable reads</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=9" title="Edit section: Repeatable reads"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAY4">In this isolation level, a lock-based <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_control" title="Concurrency control" id="mwAY8">concurrency control</a> DBMS implementation keeps read and write locks (acquired on selected data) until the end of the transaction.  However, <i id="mwAZA">range-locks</i> are not managed, so <i id="mwAZE"><b id="mwAZI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="#Phantom_reads" class="mw-selflink-fragment" id="mwAZM">phantom reads</a></b></i> can occur.</p>

<p id="mwAZQ">Write skew is possible at this isolation level in some systems. Write skew is a phenomenon where two writes are allowed to the same column(s) in a table by two different writers (who have previously read the columns they are updating), resulting in the column having data that is a mix of the two transactions.<sup about="#mwt22" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-3"}}'><a href="#cite_note-3" id="mwAZU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZc">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt25" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}'><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwAZk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAZo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZs">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAZw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="10" id="mwAZ0" aria-labelledby="Read_committed"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Read_committed">Read committed</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=10" title="Edit section: Read committed"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAZ4">In this isolation level, a lock-based <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_control" title="Concurrency control" id="mwAZ8">concurrency control</a> DBMS implementation keeps write locks (acquired on selected data) until the end of the transaction, but read locks are released as soon as the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Select_(SQL)" title="Select (SQL)" id="mwAaA">SELECT</a> operation is performed (so the <i id="mwAaE"><b id="mwAaI"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="#Non-repeatable_reads" class="mw-selflink-fragment" id="mwAaM">non-repeatable reads phenomenon</a></b></i> can occur in this isolation level). As in the previous level, <i id="mwAaQ">range-locks</i> are not managed.</p>

<p id="mwAaU">Putting it in simpler words, read committed is an isolation level that guarantees that any data read is committed at the moment it is read. It simply restricts the reader from seeing any intermediate, uncommitted, 'dirty' read. It makes no promise whatsoever that if the transaction re-issues the read, it will find the same data; data is free to change after it is read.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="11" id="mwAaY" aria-labelledby="Read_uncommitted"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Read_uncommitted">Read uncommitted</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=11" title="Edit section: Read uncommitted"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAac">This is the <i id="mwAag">lowest</i> isolation level. In this level, <i id="mwAak"><b id="mwAao"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="#Dirty_reads" class="mw-selflink-fragment" id="mwAas">dirty reads</a></b></i> are allowed, so one transaction may see <i id="mwAaw">not-yet-committed</i> changes made by other transactions.</p>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="12" id="mwAa0" aria-labelledby="Default_isolation_level"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Default_isolation_level">Default isolation level</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=12" title="Edit section: Default isolation level"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwAa4">The <i id="mwAa8">default isolation level</i> of different <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_management_system" title="Database management system" class="mw-redirect" id="mwAbA">DBMS</a>'s varies quite widely. Most databases that feature transactions allow the user to set any isolation level. Some DBMS's also require additional syntax when performing a SELECT statement to acquire locks (e.g. <i id="mwAbE">SELECT ... FOR UPDATE</i> to acquire exclusive write locks on accessed rows).</p>

<p id="mwAbI">However, the definitions above have been criticized as being ambiguous, and as not accurately reflecting the isolation provided by many databases:</p>

<dl id="mwAbM"><dd id="mwAbQ">This paper shows a number of weaknesses in the anomaly approach to defining isolation levels. The three ANSI phenomena are ambiguous, and even in their loosest interpretations do not exclude some anomalous behavior ... This leads to some counter-intuitive results. In particular, lock-based isolation levels have different characteristics than their ANSI equivalents. This is disconcerting because commercial database systems typically use locking implementations. Additionally, the ANSI phenomena do not distinguish between a number of types of isolation level behavior that are popular in commercial systems.<sup about="#mwt28" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-sql-isolation_5-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"sql-isolation"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-sql-isolation-5"}}'><a href="#cite_note-sql-isolation-5" id="mwAbU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAbY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAbc">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAbg">]</span></span></a></sup></dd></dl>

<p id="mwAbk">There are also other criticisms concerning ANSI SQL's isolation definition, in that it encourages implementors to do "bad things":</p>

<dl id="mwAbo"><dd id="mwAbs">... it relies in subtle ways on an assumption that a locking schema is used for concurrency control, as opposed to an optimistic or multi-version concurrency scheme. This implies that the proposed semantics are <i id="mwAbw">ill-defined</i>.<sup about="#mwt31" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}'><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwAb0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAb4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAb8">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAcA">]</span></span></a></sup></dd></dl>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="13" id="mwAcE" aria-labelledby="Isolation_levels_vs_read_phenomena"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Isolation_levels_vs_read_phenomena">Isolation levels vs read phenomena</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Isolation_(database_systems)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=13" title="Edit section: Isolation levels vs read phenomena"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

</tbody></table>

<p id="mwAd0">Anomaly serializable is not the same as serializable. That is, it is necessary, but not sufficient that a serializable schedule should be free of all three phenomena types.<sup about="#mwt45" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-sql-isolation_5-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"sql-isolation"}}'><a href="#cite_note-sql-isolation-5" id="mwAd4"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwAd8"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAeA">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwAeE">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
